newsitem.title: UK: HP Bulmer says brand strength boosts profit.
newsitem.headline: HP Bulmer says brand strength boosts profit.

text.p: British cider maker HP Bulmer Holdings Plc said on Wednesday that the strength of its brands helped it to push up first-half profits, despite a "fiercely competitive market."
The company said pre-tax profits and sales both jumped 19 percent, to 16.6 million stg and 162.6 million stg respectively, boosted by the acquisition of Inch's Cider Ltd in May.
Excluding Inch's, sales rose 5.2 percent. The company made an exceptional charge of 0.7 million stg for redundancies and restructuring linked to the acquisition.
In September Bulmer was hit by fallout from rival Matthew Clark Plc's warning that a new wave of drinks known as alcopops had sharply affected its sales and profits.
Bulmer said its research and experience "shows that alcopops have taken sales from a wide variety of alcoholic drinks and that the impact on its brands has not been significant."
The group said it "remains confident that the underlying market growth remains sound and has deviated little from the trend experienced in recent years."
The company said it estimated underlying cider market growth at seven percent and said its share of the UK cider market had risen to 53 percent from 50 percent in 1995.
"We believe that notwithstanding the current competitive environment, the group should continue to make satisfactory progress both at home and overseas," Bulmer added.
